critique.good: All five columns are visible at once, and the three data rows remain compact and easy to compare.
critique.problems: The header dominates the table, with narrow, jagged stacks and several visibly broken words. The metric labels are difficult to scan as phrases.
critique.cause: The 76–79px metric columns leave only 55–58px for text. That is narrower than several header words, including “Average,” “minutes,” “purchase,” and “support.”

critique.good: The wider first metric column makes its header much easier to read, and the shorter header row brings the data into view sooner. The small overflow preserves most of the table at first sight.
critique.problems: The support column is cut off at the viewport edge, so its label and values require scrolling. The headers still form tall stacks, particularly the first and third metrics.
critique.cause: The 49+100+79+88px preceding columns reach beyond the 360px viewport; the 79px support column is mostly outside it. The first and third metric columns still have only 79px and 67px of text space respectively.

critique.good: The headers have a calmer rhythm and read more naturally in short phrases. The compact header row makes each site's values easy to follow.
critique.problems: Only the site and first two metrics are initially visible; readers must scroll substantially to compare purchase and support figures. The generous width is disproportionate to the tiny data values.
critique.cause: The four metric columns total 540px, making the table 230px wider than the viewport.

critique.good: All header words and site identifiers stay intact. The compact metric columns keep the three site rows easy to scan, and the small overflow limits scrolling.
critique.problems: The header is tall and choppy, with isolated short words in the purchase header. The support column is only partly visible on first sight, so its heading and values require horizontal scrolling.
critique.cause: The 91px, 79px, 88px and 79px metric widths leave little room for phrases; the 387px total puts the last 27px beyond the viewport.

critique.good: The wider metric columns produce a shorter header and more natural phrases, particularly in the audience and session-length headings. Rows remain clear and the numbers align for comparison.
critique.problems: The support column is entirely beyond the initial viewport, making one of the four metrics easy to miss. The purchase heading still breaks into several short lines.
critique.cause: The 110px, 90px, 105px and 90px metric widths improve wrapping but increase the table to 445px; the first four columns alone occupy 354px.

critique.good: Header words stay intact, and the wider audience and support columns give those headings a little more room. The data rows retain a consistent rhythm.
critique.problems: The table is as tall as r1A but needs more scrolling, with much of the support column outside the viewport. The purchase header remains fragmented.
critique.cause: Increasing the audience column to 96px and support column to 90px does not reduce the six-line maximum, while raising the total width to 403px.

critique.good: The site labels and numeric rows are compact and easy to compare. The metric headers retain whole words, and the modest overflow keeps the first four columns largely in view.
critique.problems: The header is much taller than the data, and the purchase header has an awkward isolated “a.” The support column is mostly outside the initial viewport.
critique.cause: At 88px, the purchase column has too little text width to combine several short words comfortably. The 396px total places most of the fifth column beyond the 360px viewport.

critique.good: The wider purchase column gives that header a more coherent shape, while the numeric rows remain easy to scan.
critique.problems: The audience header is still a tall stack, and the wider purchase column pushes the support column farther out of view. Its improved wrapping does not reduce the shared header-row height.
critique.cause: The 105px purchase column uses 17px more than in r2A, while the 91px audience column remains narrow enough to require six lines. The total width is 404px.

critique.good: All five metrics and their values appear within the initial viewport, making cross-column row scanning immediate.
critique.problems: Several header words visibly split across lines, including “session,” “minutes,” “purchase,” and “opened.” The fragmented text creates a very tall, uneven header that is harder to read than the short numeric rows.
critique.cause: The 75px, 80px, and 73px metric columns leave only 54px, 59px, and 52px for text, less than their stated longest words require. The 82px audience column also leaves less than its stated 70px requirement.

understanding.purpose: Compare three sites across audience size, session length, purchase conversion and support demand.
understanding.reading: Readers scan each site’s row, then compare values down each metric column; the long headers identify otherwise compact numbers.
groups: Columns 2–4 describe audience activity and purchase behavior; column 5 describes support demand. All four are metrics attached to the site in column 1.
keep_intact: Site identifiers A, B and C
Numeric values and their units or suffixes
Header words when the available width permits
may_wrap: The four metric headers can wrap between words; their shared header row can absorb multiple lines.

bad.why: The rendered headers visibly split several words, including “session,” “minutes,” “purchase,” and “opened.” The resulting fragments and eight-line header make the table harder to scan, despite fitting the viewport.

final.rationale: r2A keeps the site labels and numeric values compact while giving the long headers enough room to retain whole words. Its 36px overflow is the smallest among the candidates that visibly preserve whole words, although the support-ticket column requires horizontal scrolling. The six-line header is tall, but the three data rows remain easy to compare. The narrow ranges are approximate and should be checked in the browser because small width changes can alter wrapping.

general: Preserving whole words in headers helps readers identify measures and compare their values.
Column widths should reflect the demands of their content and their role in the table, rather than defaulting to equal widths.
Horizontal scrolling can be worthwhile when squeezing a table would damage readability.
specific: The four measures have tiny values but unusually long headers, so header readability largely determines the width allocation.
The reported zero mid-word splits for r2C conflicts with its rendered image; the visible rendering is the basis for judging it.
At the initial viewport, part of the final measure is offscreen even in the preferred design.

final.tradeoffs: r1B and r3C offer shorter, more open headers but require substantially more sideways scrolling. r2C keeps the table within the viewport at the cost of broken words and a much taller header.
final.uncertain: A designer prioritizing an immediately visible full table might tolerate r2C, while one prioritizing relaxed header wrapping might prefer r1B. The exact equally good width ranges are uncertain without rendering further variations.

A.why: All five columns fit, but the narrow metric columns break many header words into fragments, making the measures difficult to identify.

B.why: Headers remain intact and the first four columns are readable. The fifth column straddles the viewport edge and requires a short horizontal scroll.

C.why: The first four columns have readable, intact headers and a calm rhythm, but the fifth column is entirely beyond the viewport, making it easy to miss.

D.why: The headers are readable without split words, and a sliver of the fifth column signals more content. Its values require horizontal scrolling.

E.why: The first four columns read clearly, but only a small fragment of the fifth is visible initially, so the final measure and its values require scrolling.

F.why: All five columns fit, but several headers split words across lines, including the session, purchase, and support measures. The resulting fragments slow comparison.

reviews.unsure: The screenshots show only part of the horizontally overflowing columns, so the full width and appearance of the fifth column cannot be judged precisely.

A.why: The headers wrap at word boundaries and the rows remain easy to compare, but the support column extends beyond the initial viewport.

B.why: All five columns fit, but headers split words such as “session,” “platforms” and “purchase,” making them hard to read.

C.why: The first four columns read clearly, with intact words and compact rows. The support column requires horizontal scrolling.

D.why: The first four columns have comfortable widths and readable headers, but the entire support column sits beyond the initial viewport.

E.why: The headers retain whole words, the rows scan cleanly, and most of the support column is visible initially; a small horizontal scroll is still needed.

F.why: The oversized Site column leaves the metric columns too narrow, breaking several header words and producing a tall, difficult-to-scan header.

reviews.unsure: The supplied views appear cropped at the right edge for some layouts, so the full extent and exact widths of the off-screen support columns are difficult to judge.
